install_tell: roslaunch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket.launch (ROS1) OR ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml (ROS2) — both leave ~authenticate=False by default
misconfig_patterns: ~authenticate defaults False (source-verified in ros1 branch rosbridge_websocket.py at 2026-06-09). Server accepts any WebSocket client, executes any op.
Default bind 0.0.0.0 on port 9090. Internet exposure is purely a routing/firewall question.
null_origin_allowed defaults True — browser cross-origin from arbitrary attacker JS pages is permitted.

Authentication, when enabled, requires the separate rosauth package; the operator has to flip the flag, install rosauth, and distribute a MAC token. Rarely done in practice (Issue #29 open since 2014).
TLS off by default (certfile=None, keyfile=None). When enabled, port 9090 serves wss://; older builds (pre-Issue #570) negotiate TLS 1.0/1.1.
`publish` op over WebSocket bypasses the rosmaster XML-RPC API entirely — single message can drive /cmd_vel or any other actuator topic.
`call_service` to non-/rosapi/* services invokes service handlers (nav goals, motor enable, costmap clear, etc.) — robot-motion primitive over WebSocket.
Co-deploy with web_video_server (8080) + rosmaster (11311) is the headline 'browser-controlled robot' exposure class.

active_probe.false_positive_check: rosbridge response to /rosapi/topics call is a service_response op with values.topics array and result:true. Reject if Tornado banner is the only signal (vanilla Tornado app — high FP). Reject if WS upgrade succeeds but op response is missing or is an 'unknown service' fault. Reject if 'rosapi' package not installed (rare — ships with rosbridge_suite default install). Confirm with secondary /rosapi/services + /rosapi/nodes calls returning same shape.

shodan_dorks.notes: Insight #93: basic dork is port-free and catches rosbridge relocated to non-9090 (some operators bind to 80/443/9091 behind nginx WS-proxy). Tornado server header alone is HIGH-FP because Tornado is a generic Python framework — conjunctive match with 'rosbridge' in body is required. Existing nuclei template `network/detection/rosbridge-detect.yaml` keys on WS handshake + advertise test; adapt for read-only /rosapi/topics confirm. No favicon shipped by default — favicon-hash pivot not available. roslibjs version in companion static GUI (vampire.py target) pins deployment date.

deployment_tells: Robot Web Tools stack: rosbridge_server (9090) + roslibjs (browser) + ros3djs + web_video_server (8080) — canonical 'control a robot from a browser' bundle.
TurtleBot Web GUI tutorials wire rosbridge + web_video_server on the same NUC.
Industrial telepresence: Beam, Double, Ohmni, suitable-tech derivatives (early generations ran ROS+rosbridge under the hood).
Docker-compose: `services: rosbridge: image: ros2-rosbridge ports: ['9090:9090']` — verbatim in many GitHub repos including university courseware.
Cloud robotics: AWS RoboMaker tutorials, Azure Percept robotics samples wire rosbridge.

Reverse-proxy: nginx `proxy_pass http://localhost:9090` with `Upgrade: websocket` headers — documented in RobotWebTools tutorials. Direct-IP :9090 often reachable past SNI filtering (Insight #12 shadow-port).
Co-deploy ports: 11311 (rosmaster — ROS1 only; ROS2 uses DDS discovery on 7400-7500), 8080/8181 (web_video_server), 11345 (gzserver), 22 (SSH), 5900 (VNC), 8888 (Jetson Jupyter).
TLS posture: most deployments are ws:// not wss://. When wss enabled, subject-CN often robot.<lab>.<univ>.edu — VisorGraph cert-pivot to operator portfolio.
University adopters with public rosbridge tutorials: Stanford CS324, MIT 6.141, CMU 16-311, Berkeley EECS C106B, ETH Zurich Programming for Robotics.
pivot_paths: WS / call_service /rosapi/get_param_names → parameter namespace dump (mirrors rosmaster getParamNames)
WS / call_service /rosapi/get_param → parameter value read (credential leak hotspot)
WS / subscribe to /tf, /rosout (log topic — diagnostic leakage), /joint_states (robot pose) — receive-only, set throttle_rate
HTTP GET / → Tornado identity banner + version string (where present)
vulnerabilities: Issue #29 (open since 2014) — rosbridge protocol should support generic authentication; ~authenticate=False default acknowledged.
Issue #459 — auth op handling bugs on websocket server side.
Issue #570 — TLS 1.0/1.1 still offered by older builds.
Issue #434 — auth flow regression after Autobahn → Tornado migration.
No published CVE specifically for the auth-disabled default (it is documented design, not a bug).
No CISA KEV entries as of 2026-06-09.
do_not_call: WS publish op — publishes a message on a topic; can move actual robots when sent to /cmd_vel, /joint_states, motor topics
WS advertise op — registers as publisher (preludes a publish; also pollutes node graph)
WS unadvertise op — tears down a publisher
WS advertise_service op — registers rogue service server; robot routes calls to attacker
WS unadvertise_service op — tears down a service
WS call_service to non-/rosapi/* services — invokes service handlers (nav goals, motor enable, costmap clear, etc.)
WS send_action_goal — triggers nav goals, arm trajectories
WS advertise_action / unadvertise_action — rogue action server registration
WS set_level — mutates log verbosity state
WS auth — only meaningful when ~authenticate=true; do not attempt to brute the MAC
data_class: robot topology + parameter-server contents (frequent credential/token/path leakage via /rosapi/get_param) + indirect physical-motion capability when chained with publish or call_service to actuator topics. Diagnostic topics (/rosout) can leak operational state in transit. NOT user PII directly, but exposes operational robot state, sensor streams (cameras via co-deployed web_video_server), and the means to control physical actuators.
restraint_notes: Identity probe = WS handshake + call_service /rosapi/topics only.
Topology read = call_service /rosapi/{topics, services, nodes} (three reads cover the full graph; mirrors rosmaster getSystemState).
Parameter read = /rosapi/get_param_names first; selectively /rosapi/get_param only on names suggesting secret-leak. Names ARE the finding.
NEVER call publish, advertise, advertise_service, call_service-to-non-rosapi, send_action_goal — these are robot-motion primitives.
Set throttle_rate on any subscribe op to avoid hammering operator bandwidth / camera streams.
Insight #93: pair port:9090-pinned dork with port-free Tornado+rosbridge anchor to catch reverse-proxied or relocated rosbridge.
Insight #12 shadow-sweep: every confirmed rosbridge gets a 11311 + 8080 + 11345 cross-port check on the same /32 — the 9090+8080 combo is the headline class.
Co-deployed web_video_server (8080) is a separate Lane D target — camera MJPEG streams are direct sensor exfil, no rosbridge needed.
